newsitem.title: USA: Westvaco says Q2 hurt by declining prices.
newsitem.headline: Westvaco says Q2 hurt by declining prices.

text.p: Westvaco Corp said Tuesday that second quarter earnings were hurt by lower prices for linerboard and coated papers, where there is still and industry-wide imbalance between supply and demand.

The company added that the volume of total product shipments increased three percent, quarter to quarter, average overall prices declined by eight percent, reflecting the situation with linerboard and coated paper.
But Westvaco chief executive John Luke, said "Demand has now strengthened for linerboard and coated papers, and ther are signs that this trend will continue."
He said Westvaco's bleached board and consumer packaging businesses are experiencing improving market conditions, as is its Brazilian packaging business.
Luke also said that demand for other unbleached products, including folding carton board and saturating kraft fro decorative laminates, continues to be strong.
The company said that in the future it will emphasize cost management as well as upgrading the company's product mix.

It has recently completed construction of a new activated carbon plant in Wickliffe, Ky. that will produce material for automobile emissions control and new applications such as batteries used in consunmer electronics.
The company aslo said in early July it will complete upgrades at its fine papers mill in Luke, Md.
